term: intellect not itself a body versus non-organic exercise
resolution: Q.75 a.2 makes two separate subconclusions. IntellectIsNotBody negates the body predicate of the designated intellectual principle. IntellectUsesNoBodilyOrgan denies a body related to that principle by instrumental exercise. The latter requires the separately stated organ-interference premise; it is not inferred from the former or from the old NaturalBodilyInterference constraint. The finite organInterferenceOmission theorem explicitly realizes non-bodyhood and the old interference constraint with a bodily instrument. Neither sense denies object-side bodily dependence or identifies human knowing with the highest divine immateriality.
